# Wiring an external check service into the graph

The bundled `verifier-http` executor calls a check service with a payload the
template declares. An approving answer settles the node fresh; a refusing one
fails it, carrying the service's own class.

## The template

```yaml
name: verifier-http-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: verifier
    executor: verifier-http
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:
            type: string
            default: "http://check-service:8000/pass"
          body:
            type: object
            default:
              table: items
              rows: 3
              checksum: abc123
```

No verifier is written.

## The approving route

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/nodes/$IID/verifier"
```

The node settles fresh. Its attributes record `verifier_status: 200` and
`verifier_pass: true`, and the check service receives the exact JSON object the
template declared under `attributes.body`, verbatim.

## A refusing route

Point `url` at a route answering 422 with `{"class": "schema_mismatch"}`.

The node settles with one failed run and no fresh run. The terminal class is the
upstream's own class appended to the verifier's family —
`terminal/error/verifier/check_failed/schema_mismatch` — and the recorded
payload names the actual status, the expected status
(`expected_status`), and the upstream's class.

A route answering 503 with `{"class": "upstream_down"}` settles failed the same
way with that route's class.

Both error families route to error, and both carry the upstream's own class
through to the template author's `error_types` policy.
